title: Reactions of Alcohols
content:
# Reactions of Alcohols

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe the combustion of alcohols
- Describe the oxidation of alcohols to carboxylic acids
- Describe the dehydration of alcohols to alkenes
- Write equations for the reactions of alcohols with sodium

## Introduction

Alcohols undergo several important reactions due to their -OH functional group. They can be oxidised to form aldehydes and carboxylic acids, dehydrated to form alkenes, and react with metals like sodium.

## Key Concepts

### Combustion of Alcohols

**Alcohols burn in air to produce carbon dioxide and water:**

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 3\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Properties as fuels:**
| Property | Advantage |
|----------|----------|
| Clean burning | Less pollution than petrol |
| Renewable | Can be made from crops |
| Less toxic | Safer than some fuels |
| Carbon neutral | CO₂ absorbed by growing crops |

**Alcohols as biofuels:**
- Ethanol from fermentation of sugar cane/corn
- Can be mixed with petrol (E10, E85)
- Reduces dependence on fossil fuels

### Oxidation of Alcohols

**Alcohols can be oxidised to form new products:**

**Using acidified potassium dichromate(VI):**
- K₂Cr₂O₇ / H₂SO₄
- Colour change: orange → green

**Primary alcohols → Aldehydes → Carboxylic acids:**

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$

Ethanol → Ethanal → Ethanoic acid

**[O] represents oxidation** (oxygen added or hydrogen removed)

**Full equation:**
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 2[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Natural oxidation (wine to vinegar):**
- Bacteria oxidise ethanol in wine
- Produces ethanoic acid (vinegar)

### Types of Alcohols and Oxidation

| Type | Structure | Oxidation product |
|------|-----------|------------------|
| Primary | -CH₂OH (OH on end carbon) | Aldehyde, then carboxylic acid |
| Secondary | -CHOH- (OH on middle carbon) | Ketone |
| Tertiary | -COH (OH on carbon with 3 C) | Resistant to oxidation |

### Dehydration of Alcohols

**Dehydration = removal of water**

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3, 300°C} \text{C}_2\text{H}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Ethanol → Ethene + Water

**Conditions:**
- Hot aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) catalyst
- Or concentrated sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)
- High temperature

**This is the reverse of hydration:**
- Hydration: alkene + H₂O → alcohol
- Dehydration: alcohol → alkene + H₂O

### Reaction with Sodium

**Alcohols react with sodium metal:**

$$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{H}_2$$

Ethanol + Sodium → Sodium ethoxide + Hydrogen

**Observations:**
- Sodium floats and fizzes gently
- Hydrogen gas is produced
- Much slower than sodium with water

**Why slower than with water?**
- The O-H bond in alcohols is slightly stronger
- The hydrocarbon chain reduces reactivity

### Esterification

**Alcohols react with carboxylic acids to form esters:**

$$\text{Alcohol} + \text{Carboxylic acid} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ester} + \text{Water}$$

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{COOC}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Ethanol + Ethanoic acid ⇌ Ethyl ethanoate + Water

**Conditions:**
- Concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst
- Heat under reflux

(Esters are covered in more detail in a later lesson)

### Summary of Alcohol Reactions

| Reaction | Reagent | Product | Conditions |
|----------|---------|---------|------------|
| Combustion | O₂ | CO₂ + H₂O | Burning |
| Oxidation | K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄ | Carboxylic acid | Heat |
| Dehydration | Al₂O₃ or H₂SO₄ | Alkene | Heat |
| With sodium | Na | Sodium alkoxide + H₂ | Room temp |
| Esterification | Carboxylic acid | Ester | H₂SO₄ catalyst, heat |

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** Write the equation for the complete combustion of methanol.

**Solution:**
- Methanol: CH₃OH
- Products: CO₂ and H₂O

$$2\text{CH}_3\text{OH} + 3\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

---

**Example 2:** Describe how ethanol can be converted to ethanoic acid.

**Solution:**
- Add acidified potassium dichromate(VI) solution to ethanol
- Heat the mixture
- The orange dichromate is reduced to green Cr³⁺ ions
- Ethanol is oxidised first to ethanal, then to ethanoic acid

$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 2[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Colour change:** Orange to green

---

**Example 3:** Write the equation for the dehydration of propan-1-ol.

**Solution:**
- Propan-1-ol: C₃H₇OH
- Dehydration removes H₂O
- Product is propene (C₃H₆)

$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3} \text{C}_3\text{H}_6 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Conditions: Hot aluminium oxide catalyst

---

**Example 4:** Explain why ethanol is considered carbon neutral when used as a fuel.

**Solution:**
- Ethanol is made by fermentation of glucose from plants
- The plants absorb CO₂ from the atmosphere during photosynthesis
- When ethanol burns, it releases CO₂
- The CO₂ released equals the CO₂ absorbed during growth
- Net CO₂ addition to atmosphere is zero
- Therefore, ethanol is carbon neutral

(In practice, some CO₂ is released in production and transport)

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Writing [O] as oxygen gas O₂
- **Correct:** [O] represents oxidation, not necessarily molecular oxygen

- **Mistake:** Confusing dehydration with dehydrogenation
- **Correct:** Dehydration removes H₂O; dehydrogenation removes H₂

- **Mistake:** Thinking alcohols react vigorously with sodium
- **Correct:** The reaction is gentle compared to water with sodium

## Practice Questions

1. Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of propan-1-ol. (2 marks)

2. Describe how you could oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid. Include observations. (4 marks)

3. Write the equation for the dehydration of ethanol. State the conditions. (3 marks)

4. Write the equation for the reaction of ethanol with sodium. (2 marks)

5. Explain what is meant by ethanol being a 'carbon neutral' fuel. (3 marks)

6. Name the products when butan-1-ol is:
   a) Completely combusted (1 mark)
   b) Oxidised (1 mark)
   c) Dehydrated (1 mark)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Oxidation | Gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen |
| Dehydration | Removal of water from a compound |
| Biofuel | Fuel made from biological materials |
| Carbon neutral | No net addition of CO₂ to the atmosphere |
| Esterification | Reaction of alcohol with carboxylic acid to form ester |

## Summary

- **Combustion:** Alcohol + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O (clean burning, biofuel)
- **Oxidation:** Alcohol + [O] → Carboxylic acid (using K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄)
- **Dehydration:** Alcohol → Alkene + H₂O (Al₂O₃ or H₂SO₄, heat)
- **With sodium:** Alcohol + Na → Sodium alkoxide + H₂ (gentle fizzing)
- **Esterification:** Alcohol + Carboxylic acid ⇌ Ester + Water
- **Ethanol as fuel:** Renewable, carbon neutral, burns cleanly
